metadata.title: Replication package of 'Systematic Detection of Energy Regressions in Software Version Histories'
metadata.description:
This upload includes the energy measurements results collected using the EnergyTrackr pipeline, supporting the paper Systematic Detection of Energy Regressions in Software Version Histories, submitted to the Green Software Evolution special issue of the Information and Software Technology journal.

The dataset aims to facilitate reproducibility and future research on energy-aware software development and the identification of energy regressions. The analysis covers 5 projects: Classgraph, Fastexcel, Maker, Modelmapper and Simple-OpenAI. Each project directory contains the configuration files used for both algorithms, along with two subdirectories: dichotomous-data and naive-data. These subdirectories include all generated data obtained through the respective algorithms. Each subdirectory contains 4 files: a CSV file with raw data, a CSV file with sorted raw data, an HTML file generated by EnergyTrackr, and a log file containing all execution logs.

metadata.title: Replication package for "Do Gains from Asymmetric Volatility Specifications Persist in Tail-Risk Forecasting?"
metadata.description:
Replication package for the manuscript "Do Gains from Asymmetric Volatility Specifications Persist in Tail-Risk Forecasting?" by Hongfei Guo, J. Miguel Marín, and Helena Veiga.

This archive provides model forecasts, evaluation code, random-number settings, Stan specifications, machine-readable results, and scripts that reproduce Tables 1–4, Figure 1, and the evaluation-based results in the online appendix. The default workflow begins with the released forecast panels and source index data obtained independently by the replicator; monthly model estimation is not rerun.

The daily index data were obtained from Yahoo Finance and are not redistributed because they remain subject to the provider's terms of use. The archive documents the tickers, sample periods, required input structure, and return transformation. Users must obtain the source observations directly from Yahoo Finance or another licensed provider.

metadata.title: Ferrometer
metadata.description:
An open-source, Tree-sitter-based static analysis tool that measures macro usage across Rust codebases. It classifies macro definitions and invocations into four categories (declarative, derive, attribute, function-like), tags each as standard-library or ecosystem in origin, and computes per-project invocation density.

This is the replication package for:

How Rust Projects Use Macros: A Large-Scale Empirical Study
Leopoldo Teixeira, Nilo Drumond
20th Brazilian Symposium on Software Components, Architectures, and Reuse (SBCARS 2026), co-located with CBSoft 2026

Included in this archive:

  • The tool source code (Rust, built on Tree-sitter)
  • The Python analysis and statistics scripts (aggregation, Kruskal–Wallis/Mann–Whitney tests, table and report generation)
  • The frozen corpus lockfile and analysis outputs (99 repositories, 4,001 crates, 2,215,517 macro invocations)
  • The classifier-validation pipeline and results (200-item stratified inter-rater sample, κ = 0.917 agreement)
  • A Docker image for reproducing each research question independently, with no local toolchain required

Please use the README.md for full documentation, including instructions to reproduce each of the paper's research questions.

Released under the MIT license (see LICENSE.txt on this repository).

metadata.title: Artifacts of Evaluating Shaker for Flaky Test Detection in Python Projects
metadata.description:
Replication package for the paper "Evaluating Shaker for Flaky Test Detection in Python Projects", published at SAST 2026, the 11th Brazilian Symposium on Systematic and Automated Software Testing.

The paper evaluates Shaker, a flaky-test detector that injects CPU and memory stress to amplify non-determinism, on Python for the first time. It compares Shaker against a budget-matched plain re-execution baseline ("ReRun") on 137 ground-truth flaky tests taken from the dataset of Gruber et al., and reports a null result: at an equal budget of 100 executions per test, stress injection detects no more flaky tests than simply rerunning them (37.2% against 35.8%, McNemar exact p = 0.84). Fewer than half of the ground-truth tests reproduced on independent hardware at all (45.3%), and those that did are dominated by randomness and network flakiness rather than the concurrency Shaker targets.

CONTENTS

analysis/    Scripts that rebuild every table and figure in the paper from the shipped result CSVs.
experiment/  Docker orchestration runner and results parser used to execute the study.
docker/      Two images: one for the analysis, one for test execution under stress.
shaker_py/   The Shaker tool, modified for this study. See shaker_py/NOTICE for the exact changes.
dataset/     Study inputs: ground truth, manual flakiness labels, project list, runner inputs.
results/     The two parsed result CSVs behind the paper's numbers.
raw_results/ A partial snapshot of the raw per-test output trees.
paper.pdf    The accepted paper.

REPRODUCING THE PAPER

With Docker installed, running ./run_analysis.sh from the root of the artifact rebuilds every table and figure of the paper into ./output/. It takes about a minute, needs no Python on the host, executes no tests, and requires no network access at run time. A plain Python virtualenv route producing byte-identical output is documented as well.

The expected headline numbers are Shaker 51/137 (37.2%), ReRun 49/137 (35.8%), McNemar exact p = 0.839, which are the values reported in the paper's abstract and in Table 1.

The README also documents the optional path that re-runs the experiments themselves, in isolated Docker containers under Shaker's stress and under the ReRun baseline. That path takes days of compute and saturates the host machine by design.

REQUIREMENTS

For the analysis, either Docker alone, or Python 3.10 or newer with scipy, pandas, and matplotlib. Roughly 50 MB of disk for the artifact and 550 MB for the analysis image. Re-running the experiments additionally needs a Docker daemon, network access, and several GB of disk.

DATA AND ETHICS

The artifact contains no personal, human-subject, or otherwise sensitive data. All data are execution metadata (pass/fail verdicts, run counts, and repository size metrics) for the automated test suites of publicly available open-source Python packages published on PyPI. The subject projects are not redistributed: the experiment clones each one from its own public repository at the commit recorded in dataset/projects.csv, and each remains under its own licence.

LICENSING

Code (analysis/, experiment/, docker/, shaker_py/, and the shell scripts) is released under the BSD 2-Clause License. Data (dataset/, results/, raw_results/) is released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence, matching the licence of the dataset of Gruber et al. from which the ground-truth files derive. See the LICENSE file at the root of the artifact for the full text, the scope of each licence, and the third-party attributions.

RELATED RESOURCES

Development repository: https://github.com/STAR-RG/shaker-python-sast2026
Upstream Shaker: https://github.com/STAR-RG/shaker and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5347973
Ground-truth dataset of Gruber et al.: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4450435

metadata.title: Replication package for "Measuring Defence in Depth: Coalition and Cost Analysis of a Three-Tier Web IPS"
metadata.description:
Replication package for the paper "Measuring Defence in Depth: Coalition and Cost Analysis of a Three-Tier Web IPS" (companion submission, SOICT 2026). It contains everything needed to rebuild every number in the paper: no retraining, no threshold tuning, seed 42 throughout, and no wall-clock, network access or random source other than that seed.

Three score tables: 964 mutation variants with per-tier decisions and raw EBM and Isolation Forest scores; 5,801 log hold-out requests (150 attack, 5,651 benign) with scores and keyword flags; and 17,985 CSIC-2010 records scored zero-shot. Two scripts: rebuild_all.py, which reproduces the coalition lattices, the cluster-bootstrap intervals, the threshold sweep and the two-tier cost frontier from those tables alone; and verify_numbers.py, which re-derives every arithmetic claim in the paper and prints one OK/FAIL line per check.

The tables release derived quantities only. Neither the log hold-out table nor the CSIC predictions contains request text — only scores and binary flags — and CSIC-2010 itself is not redistributed, only per-record predictions keyed to it. The mutation corpus is synthetic: semantics-preserving obfuscations of publicly documented payloads.

Requires Python 3 and the standard library only.

creators.name: MAI, HOANG DINH
creators.affiliation: Ho Chi Minh City Open University

metadata.title: Replication package for "Latency optimization and oracle-based failure diagnosis in interactive adaptive learning pipelines"
metadata.description:
Reference implementation, benchmark harness and complete measurement scripts for an oracle-localised measurement study of the recommendation critical path of Coglica, a research platform for game-based cognitive assessment.

The package reproduces every table and figure in the accompanying article: the oracle substitution that localises the lost value to the predictor rather than to the architecture; the sweep of the two interacting configuration choices inside the predictor; the latency decomposition and the cost model fitted under four serving runtimes; the closed-form enumeration/search crossover and its validation; the comparison of search strategies including stronger model-based baselines; the concurrency sweep against the synchronous and asynchronous deadlines; and the degradation chain measured in a domain metric rather than as an availability rate.

No human-subject data are used. Every domain-metric result is a simulation against a reconstructed response model; see README.md for the reconstruction's fidelity checks and limitations.

metadata.title: Replication package for: Integrative AOP-Based Mechanistic Profiling of Organic UV Filters Reveals Shared Endocrine-Metabolic and Stress-Response Pathways
metadata.description:
This repository contains the R scripts, input data, and pre-computed results supporting the analyses and figures presented in:

Integrative AOP-Based Mechanistic Profiling of Organic UV Filters Reveals Shared Endocrine-Metabolic and Stress-Response Pathways
Cristina Accardi et al. - Environmental Health, 2026.

Overview
The pipeline identifies human gene targets of 23 organic UV-filter chemicals from three evidence sources: bioassay data (PubChem, ToxCast), molecular docking predictions, and transcription-factor regulatory networks. Moreover it maps the gene target onto Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) Key Events using the AOPfingerprintR framework. Results are visualised as a consensus-coloured interactive network. GTEx v8 expression data are used to contextualise gene targets across relevant human tissues (skin, liver, breast, brain).

Contents

  • Scripts/ - four R scripts (Build_TF_reference.R, Main.R, GTEx_analysis.R, Functions_for_working_code.R)
  • Data/ - all input data files required to reproduce the analysis
  • Results/ - pre-computed outputs including enrichment tables, figures, and an interactive HTML network
  • Supplementary files/ - The outputs indicated in the Supplementary material of the manuscript 

How to reproduce
Run the scripts in order: Build_TF_reference.R → Main.R → GTEx_analysis.R. See README.md for installation instructions and exact package versions.

Software
R 4.3.1 — key packages: tidyverse 2.0.0, biomaRt 2.58.2, AOPfingerprintR 0.0.1, igraph 2.0.3, visNetwork 2.1.4, gtexr 0.2.1.

The zenodo_v2/ directory contains the expanded replication package prepared during peer-review revision. It includes the new reference-chemical benchmark, independent transcriptomic comparisons, supporting analyses, updated documentation, and pre-computed outputs.

Overview
The post-review package extends the original UV-filter workflow in two complementary ways:

  1. Framework-derived reference-chemical benchmark — analysis of eight mechanistically diverse reference chemicals using gene sets assembled from bioassay, molecular-docking, and TF-propagation evidence.
  2. Independently measured transcriptomic comparison — analysis of public differential-expression datasets for phenobarbital, etoposide, and rifampicin using the same KE-enrichment framework.

The two analyses address different questions and should not be used interchangeably. The framework-derived benchmark evaluates the complete molecular-evidence integration workflow, whereas the transcriptomic comparison evaluates KE recovery using independently measured gene-expression signatures.

New analyses

  • Benchmark using eight mechanistically diverse reference chemicals
  • Corrected mechanistic-domain classification and Supplementary Figure S1
  • Chemical-supported network-connectivity analysis
  • Generic adverse-outcome convergence analysis
  • Traceability of enriched KEs to selected named AOP-Wiki entries
  • Descriptive attribution of bioassay, docking, and TF-propagation evidence across significant chemical-KE pairs
  • Supporting bioassay-provenance, potency, activity-call, species, and assay-quality summaries
  • Reference-chemical gene-set-size comparison
  • Public transcriptomic pipelines for phenobarbital, etoposide, and rifampicin
  • Pre-computed KE-enrichment and network results for the measured transcriptomic signatures
  • Complete script-to-input and script-to-output documentation
